title: Death of man who shot police dog being examined
article: A coroner's inquest will examine the circumstances surrounding the death of Saskatoon businessman Keldon McMillan, who was shot by police during a roadside confrontation last May.

McMillan, 33, was shot after aiming a pistol at police following a high-speed car chase that ended east of Saskatoon on Highway 41 near Wakaw. McMillan had fired several shots into the air and had shot and killed a police dog sent to subdue him.
An RCMP major crimes unit investigation of the incident resulted in no criminal charges being laid against any of the 11 members of the Saskatoon city police and RCMP who were on the scene.
The date and place of the inquest have not been set.
McMillan's family was informed of the inquest last week and are anxious for it to begin, Cheryl McMillan, Keldon's sister, said Monday.
"I hope the truth comes out. We want to know what happened," she said.
"There's a bunch of whys, why couldn't they have brought in a mediator? They moved in too soon," she said.

The incident began on May 17 when police were called to McMillan's house on Beerling Crescent in Silverspring. They intended to seize illegally stored firearms and serve him with an order barring him from contact with his wife.
When McMillan returned to the house, police were stationed at the end of the block. He did not get out of his truck but drove through his yard and sped out of the city.
Three city police cars followed as he drove east, heading north on Highway 41. His vehicle was disabled by an RCMP spike belt about 10 kilometres outside of Wakaw.

Police have said McMillan got out of the truck and fired warning shots. He ignored commands to drop his handgun and shot a police dog when it attacked him. When McMillan pointed the gun at police, he was shot and killed.
McMillan's family has questioned the police actions, asking why they closed in on McMillan instead of backing off and calling in a family member to talk to him and calm him down.
